---
title: Authentication
description: API keys, bearer tokens, and the difference between sandbox and production credentials.
---

Every request carries a credential. Most integrations use an **API key**; dashboard sessions and team-management integrations use OAuth 2.0.

## API keys

Send the key in the `X-Api-Key` header. Keys are scoped to a project and an environment.

```http title="Request"
GET /v1/inboxes HTTP/1.1
Host: api.testinbox.email
X-Api-Key: tib_sandbox_0123abcd
```

| Environment | Prefix          | Mail leaves the sandbox |
| ----------- | --------------- | ----------------------- |
| Sandbox     | `tib_sandbox_`  | No                      |
| Production  | `tib_live_`     | Yes                     |

<Callout type="warning" title="Keep keys out of the browser">
API keys are secrets. Use them from CI and servers only; never embed them in front-end code or commit them to a repository.
</Callout>

## Bearer tokens

Short-lived tokens issued by the dashboard work everywhere an API key does. They expire after one hour.

## OAuth 2.0

Team-management operations such as [Invite team member](/api/team/invite-team-member) require the `team:write` scope through the authorization-code flow. The [Create webhook](/api/webhooks/create-webhook) operation shows how scopes combine with a key.

<Callout type="danger" title="Rotating a leaked key">
Revoke the key in the dashboard first, then rotate the secret in your CI provider. Revocation is immediate; in-flight requests fail with `401`.
</Callout>
